title: High bone turnover pathophysiology and the FGF23 axis
guide: CKD-MBD (previously renal osteodystrophy). High turnover (30%): osteitis fibrosa cystica; GFR ↓↓ → ↑ P; endothelial cells convert to osteoblasts → trap Ca → irreversible medial vascular calcification. Osteocytes secrete FGF23 (phosphaturic) via klotho receptor → blocks Na-P cotransporter PCT2a → phosphate excretion; actions: LVH, 1,2-hydroxylase inhibition → calcitriol deficient → hypocalcemia → secondary hyperparathyroidism (hypocalcemia, hypophosphatemia); grade 5 CKD: klothoreceptor resistance. ↑ bone formation << ↑ bone resorption; amorphous Ca₃(PO₄)₂ → trivial trauma fracture (↓ mineralization); bone + fibrous tissue + cyst → osteitis fibrosa cystica.

title: Low bone turnover and the CKD-MBD Venn triad
guide: Low turnover (10%): adynamic bone disease — middle to elderly aged female, DM, obese; prone for calcification. Venn diagram: biochemical changes + bone abnormality + calcification (vascular + soft tissue).

title: Target values, phosphate binders and tertiary hyperparathyroidism
guide: High turnover → medial calcification: ↑ P, ↑ Ca₃(PO₄)₂, ↑ PTH. Targets: PTH 2-7× ULN (50-100 pg/ml), Ca <9.5, P <5.5. 1st line pure binders: sevelamer carbonate 400 mg TDS (↓ LDL), ferric citrate, sucroferric oxyhydroxide; calcium binders only in significant hypocalcemia (may worsen calcification); calcitriol 0.25 µg alternate days (vit D <20). Tertiary HPT: autonomous nodule after long-standing 2° HPT → PTH ↑↑↑, ↑ Ca⁺ ↑ P (Ca always low in CKD except tertiary); Rx cinacalcet (CaSR agonist) → parathyroidectomy if unresponsive.

title: Adynamic bone disease and extraskeletal calcification
guide: Adynamic: worst prognosis, bone pain. Causes: excess Ca supplementation (PTH <400 pg → high Ca & P → vascular/soft tissue calcification → death) and aluminum (dialysis dementia). Extraskeletal calcification in CRF: arterial, pulmonary, periarticular. Treatment: stop all supplements; dialysis in low calcium dialysate.

title: DEXA, calciphylaxis, NSF and atheroembolic disease
guide: DEXA assesses bone mass; low bone mass → bisphosphonates; Ca/vit D with caution. Calciphylaxis (calcific uremic arteriolopathy): medial calcification of subcutaneous/dermal arterioles; precipitated by vit-K antagonist (vit-K regenerates matrix Gla protein); pulse preserved; female obese; ischemic necrosis of dermis/subcut fat; violaceous painful plaque → nodule → ulcer on buttock/trunk; livedo reticularis-like rare; clinical diagnosis; poor prognosis (secondary infection); Rx vit-K + sodium thiosulfate. NSF (scleroderma-like): gadolinium-based contrast, GFR <30 — finger contracture, swelling/fibrosis, peau d'orange. Atheroembolic renal disease: blue toes.

title: CVD in CKD: non-traditional causes, features, MI and transplant
guide: >>Leading cause of mortality: ESRD 50% cardiac deaths; young CKD 500× risk vs controls. Non-traditional: uremic toxins (uremic cardiomyopathy), medial calcification, LVH (HFpEF), endothelial dysfunction (ADMA ↑ → NO ↓, loss of fetuin), malnutrition-inflammation-nephrosclerosis (insulin resistance, protein-energy malnutrition). Arteries: endothelial dysfunction, medial calcification, ↑ wall thickness → ↑ carotid systolic BP, ↓ augmented pulse velocity. Heart: LVH, myocardial fibrosis, uremic cardiomyopathy. Flower: CKD-MBD, endothelial dysfunction, protein carbamylation, oxidative stress, uremic toxins, gut dysbiosis. Treat early: early dialysis, phosphate binders early, transplant before calcification. Uremia → pericarditis, hyperkalemia → arrhythmias. MI marker: Trop-I rate of rise, ↑20% in 9 hours (most specific). Transplant pre-requisites: iliac vessel doppler, peripheral artery doppler, CT for calcification → normal → coronary angiogram. Oxidative stress: malnutrition, bacterial products in dialysate, CKD, blood-membrane interactions, loss of antioxidants during dialysis.
